title.rendered: Songs at Midnight: Praise in the Prison | The Thankful Heart, Day 9

excerpt.rendered: In Acts 16:25-26 Paul and Silas sang hymns in prison at midnight and the chains fell off. Day 9 of The Thankful Heart learns to sing in the dark.

content.rendered:
Their backs were bleeding and their feet were in stocks. It was the darkest hour of the darkest place. And that is exactly where Paul and Silas started to sing.

The Gospel For Today | Monday, November 23, 2026 | The Thankful Heart, Day 9

Today’s Scripture

“But at midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them. Suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken; and immediately all the doors were opened and everyone’s chains were loosed.”
Acts 16:25-26 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Paul and Silas had done nothing wrong. They had set a young slave girl free from a spirit that her owners were using for profit. In return, they were dragged before the magistrates, stripped, beaten with rods and thrown into the inner prison with their feet fastened in stocks. If anyone had a reason to complain, it was these two men in Philippi.

Instead, Luke writes, “But at midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God.” Midnight is the hour when everything feels heaviest. Pain is louder. Fear is bigger. It is the hour many of us know well: lying awake over a diagnosis, a debt, a child far from home. And in exactly that hour, two wounded men lifted their voices in praise.

They were not singing because they had been set free. They sang before anything changed. Their praise was not based on their circumstances but on their God. They knew that the Lord who had sent them to Macedonia was still with them in the cell. The psalmist wrote that the Lord commands His lovingkindness in the daytime, and in the night His song is with him (Psalm 42:8). The song was already in them before the earthquake came.

And look who was listening: “the prisoners were listening to them.” Thanksgiving in a dark place is never wasted. People are watching how believers respond to suffering. Your song in the hard season may be the very thing a colleague in Sao Paulo or a neighbour in Nairobi needs to hear. Before the night was over, the jailer and his whole household had believed in the Lord Jesus.

Then came the earthquake. “Immediately all the doors were opened and everyone’s chains were loosed.” Not only Paul’s and Silas’s chains. Everyone’s. Praise does not twist God’s arm, but it does put us in agreement with the One who sets captives free. Jesus has already proclaimed liberty to the captives (Luke 4:18). Whatever your midnight looks like, you can sing into it, because the freedom has already been won.

How the Thankful Heart Sings in the Dark

It praises before the doors open. Paul and Silas sang while their feet were still in stocks.

It knows others are listening. Thanks in a hard place becomes a witness to everyone nearby.

It agrees with the freedom Christ has won. Jesus came to proclaim liberty to the captives, and praise says Amen.

Declaration

Lord, I thank You that in the night Your song is with me (Psalm 42:8). Even in my midnight hour I will pray and sing praises to You, because You are with me and You are good. I thank You that Jesus has proclaimed liberty to the captives and set me free (Luke 4:18), and that because the Son has made me free, I am free indeed (John 8:36). I lift my voice before I see the doors open, because my freedom is already won in Christ. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
